answer: An agent registry for quartz and onyx trading can require each key to maintain a unique 10 GB encoded dataset and answer unpredictable storage audits. The encoding binds data to the key, so copies cannot satisfy audits for additional identities. This makes a spiral of registrations consume proportionally more storage, provided audit deadlines make recomputation impractical. The limitation is that attackers with cheap disks can still operate many identities.
